headline: Spain Presses Belgium Into Submission
story: Spain's dominion was suffocating from the start. They pressed high across 11.4 phases, forced 37 turnovers, and recovered possession at a relentless 11.6 seconds average. Belgium had no answer. A fortunate goal at 41 minutes—a scrap of an attempt worth just 0.13 xG—offered fleeting respite, but Spain's 62% possession never loosened its grip. Fabián Ruiz orchestrated from midfield; the Belgians were asphyxiated.

The numbers exposed the chasm: Spain's 2.2 expected goals to Belgium's 0.34 was the match's only real narrative. Pau Cubarsí and Rodri Hernández, both rated 7.3–7.5, controlled tempo while Courtois faced just two on-target shots before Spain's clinical 88th-minute finish (0.69 xG). Belgium's 40 forced turnovers were hollow—they lacked the precision to convert desperation into danger. Spain's ball recovery advantage and relentless pressing had already decided it.

keyMoment.text: Spain's late goal sealed it; two hours of press intensity became, at last, inevitable.

home.verdict: Relentless pressing dictated everything; survived one low-probability scare at 41.
points: Pressed high across 11.4 phases, forcing 37 turnovers while controlling 62 percent possession.
Ball recovery time of 11.6 seconds exhausted Belgium's 20-second struggle; midfield dominance was total.
Rodri and Cubarsí's 7.3–7.5 ratings anchored defence; limited opponent to 0.34 xG across ninety minutes.

away.verdict: Outmatched in possession and tempo; their one goal proved woefully insufficient.
points: Needed sharper finishing: 0.34 xG spoke to limited creation; one fortunate goal at 41 minutes was insufficient.
Ball recovery time doubled Spain's (20s versus 11.6s); pressed by only 2.8 high-press phases against 11.4.
Only five shots—two on target—against Spain's seventeen exposed toothless attack; early urgency was critical.

statLine: Spain recovered possession in 11.6 seconds versus Belgium's 20-second scramble; attrition became suffocation.
